newsitem.title: UK: UK grain futures firm in low-volume trade.
newsitem.headline: UK grain futures firm in low-volume trade.

text.p: The UK grain futures ended firm but in a market that was reported "deadly quiet" on Friday with active trade sidelined by a freight convention in London.
A firmer pound and Thursday's unspectacular EU tender let the market sleep on in the morning, but business revived a little in the afternoon session.
"After reaching around 2.50 in the morning then dropping below 2.48 against the deutschemark, sterling is helping to hold the market back," one trader said.
Wheat futures ended 0.35 to 0.50 stg up with November at 94.75 on a turnover of 180 lots and barley closed unchanged with just seven lots traded.
Amsterdam milling wheat futures also ended unchanged with no firm trades.
Cash grain told the same story.
"Nobody seems to be the slightest bit interested today," one market source said.
The UK FOB sector was neglected with little business reported.
Trading on the delivered market was subdued.
Norfolk/Suffolk feedwheat for December delivery fetched 98.00 stg a tonne and November feed barley to Liverpool saw 100.00 to 101.00 stg a tonne.
